newPageBriefs.contributionAndEvidence: Decision gap: readers compare offers quoted in different periods and do not see how hours worked change the effective hourly rate. Basis: calculated (pure arithmetic from reader inputs; no external figures). Reference code and output saved (paycheck-reference-calc.py, salary cases incl. 52,000 -> 25.00). Visible attribution: 'In our internal modeling, we converted the same $60,000 salary across 35 to 45 hour weeks to show how the hourly rate moves.' Counterexample: unpaid weeks or overtime change the conversion; page states they are not modeled. WRITE/AUDIT guardrail: the 35 to 45 hour table is plain arithmetic, so present it as an illustration/sensitivity aid, not original research or a finding; Phase 4 tests default 40x52, 37.5 hours, and period conversions with its own replay.

newPageBriefs.takeaway: Conversion is arithmetic on the reader's hours: salary / (hours x weeks) = hourly. Applies to any pay offer; the answer changes if hours, unpaid weeks or overtime differ. Gross figure is not take-home; for that, use the paycheck calculator. Informational page, no purchase recommendation.

newPageBriefs.contributionAndEvidence: Decision gap: readers see gross pay but not what survives federal and payroll tax. Basis: calculated from IRS figures (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 brackets; IRS 2026 release standard deduction $16,100 single / $32,200 MFJ / $24,150 HoH; IRS Topic 751 rates and $184,500 wage base; Topic 560 0.9% above $200,000). Reference code with hand-check ($60,000 single: federal $5,020, SS $3,720, Medicare $870, net $50,390) saved. Attribution: 'In our internal modeling, we ran 2026 federal brackets and payroll tax across salaries from $40,000 to $150,000 to estimate take-home pay.' Counterexample: state tax or a W-4 with extra withholding makes the check smaller; stated. Unknown: actual employer withholding method (IRS Pub 15-T) differs from annual liability. WRITE/AUDIT guardrails: (a) model employer withholding of 0.9% Additional Medicare above $200,000 for all statuses (IRS Topic 751) and say a married couple's final liability uses Topic 560 thresholds ($250,000 MFJ, $125,000 MFS, $200,000 others) and can differ; (b) pre-tax input is a traditional 401(k)/403(b)-style deferral that lowers income tax only, FICA stays on gross; Section 125 premiums, HSA and similar deductions not modeled; (c) 'What This Estimate Leaves Out' names tips, overtime, senior and QBI deductions, child tax credit, credits generally, state/local tax, W-4 extra withholding; result is an annual-liability estimate, not IRS Pub 15-T withholding; (d) wage base cited to IRS Topic 751 (SSA blocked curl); (e) Phase 4 replay with own artifact: std-deduction boundary ($16,100 single = $0 federal), SS cap above $184,500, MFJ and HoH cases, 26/24/52/12 period defaults.
newPageBriefs.tablesToolsVisuals: Inputs: gross pay + period, pay frequency, filing status (single, MFJ, HoH; MFS excluded), pre-tax retirement contribution (reduces income tax only, not FICA). Outputs: annual and per-paycheck federal tax, Social Security, Medicare, net. Reuses src/lib/tax-bracket.ts constants (already match Rev. Proc. 2025-32). Table of sourced constants; modeled salary table. Standard deduction only; no credits.
newPageBriefs.testingAndReview: Site _experience.md section G licenses product testing only; a calculator is not a product test and finance is excluded, so ordinary presentation: no 'we tested', howWeTested or tested schema. Math is labeled calculated; scenarios labeled modeling. Review profile HIGH (consequential tax/financial claims): 2 independent audits max, no professionalReviewRequired (general educational estimator, no individualized advice).
newPageBriefs.takeaway: Single filer at $60,000 keeps about $50,390 a year before state tax, roughly 84% of gross. Applies to W-2 employees using the standard deduction; answer changes with state tax, itemizing, credits, extra W-4 withholding or health premiums. Estimate, not withholding advice; consult payroll or a tax professional for exact figures.
